solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Out of date medicine that is valued 50% off

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, keeping only its front three of six letters

explanation.surface: Expired medicine whose valuation has been slashed by half.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' keeps the first half of 'valued', VAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hopelessly old-fashioned is called medieval, as if belonging to the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Flicks mane initially over jockeys

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
to jockey for position is to vie, so jockeys means vies

explanation.surface: A horse's mane flicking about as jockeys ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flicks' is old slang for films at the cinema, not a flick of the mane.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicks is informal for cinema films, the pictures.

clue.text: Coat and red pants — Edward's dressed

indicators.note: pants as British slang for rubbish suggests a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Edward kitted out in a coat and red trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is a verb-like noun in the surface (trousers) but signals the anagram, as in British slang 'pants' means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorated and dressed both mean adorned, as a shop window or tree is dressed.

clue.text: Go in two parts of a hospital

parts.note: the first of the two hospital parts is ENT, the ear, nose and throat department
the second part is ER, the emergency room

explanation.surface: Visiting two wards of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department and ER the emergency room, two familiar hospital sections.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go into it, the plain verb sense.

clue.text: Stayed away from a very old fish on bottom of pond

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

indicators.note: bottom of means the final letter in this down clue, the one at the foot

explanation.surface: An ancient fish lurking on the floor of a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoided means kept clear of, the same as stayed away from.

clue.text: The woman's embracing old English men of bravery

indicators.note: embracing means the possessive word holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: belonging to the woman is hers

explanation.surface: A woman hugging some brave old-fashioned Englishmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroes are people admired for courage, so the plural noun matches brave men.

clue.text: Harassed after former lover spoke

indicators.note: after means the harried word comes behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
pressed means harried or harassed

explanation.surface: Someone speaking up after being hounded by an old flame.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressed means put into words, much as spoke means said.

clue.text: Time after work for musical drama

indicators.note: after means the time period follows the work abbreviation

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Time off after work for an evening at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a drama set to music, sung throughout.

clue.text: South American writers echo doubt

parts.note: US means American, as in US citizens
pens are writing instruments
Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: Novelists from South America echoing uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of anxious uncertainty, the doubt of not yet knowing.

clue.text: Work? Love to go for a holiday

indicators.note: to go for means one letter departs and another takes its place

parts.note: a vocation is one's calling or line of work
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone deciding to swap their work for a romantic break.
explanation.walkthrough: In VOCATION the O (love) is replaced by A, giving the new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacation is the American word for a holiday, a period away from work or study.

clue.text: Had a leak during steamship races

indicators.note: during means the slang verb sits within the ship's two letters

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
slang: to have a leak is to urinate, so this is peed

explanation.surface: A passenger relieving himself while aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Races as a verb means goes very fast, the same as speeds.

clue.text: Tickled? Am leaving, mistreated

indicators.note: leaving means the little word departs from the start of the longer word

parts.note: tickled means amused, as in tickled pink

explanation.surface: Someone who was tickled now feels badly treated and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in the sense of exploited means taken advantage of, badly treated.

clue.text: Dread removing top to reveal boob

indicators.note: removing top means the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: dread is terror, great fear

explanation.surface: Fear of exposing oneself after taking off a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boob' is British slang for a blunder, not the body part the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob in British slang is a silly mistake, a blunder.

clue.text: Hopeless repositioning tree with spade

indicators.note: repositioning means the letters of the two nouns are moved into new places

explanation.surface: A gardener despairing over moving a tree with only a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate situation is one beyond hope, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Dull sanctimonious talk boring sexually active man

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the short word goes inside the other

parts.note: a stud is a man with a busy sex life
pi, short for pi-jaw, is sanctimonious or preachy talk

explanation.surface: Preachy chatter wearying a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' here means slow-witted, not tedious; PI is pi-jaw, a schoolboy word for moralising talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull in the sense of slow-witted or dim describes someone lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Dressing and cooking before shaving?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a paring is a thin shaving cut off something

explanation.surface: Getting dressed and making breakfast before a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing a salad or bird and cooking a meal are both ways of getting food ready; the question mark flags the split 'pre-paring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing and cooking food are both ways of getting it ready to eat.

clue.text: Talk about athletic contest with son

parts.note: the discus is a throwing event in athletics
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A parent chatting about a sports meeting with their boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk about a topic is to debate or consider it, the same as the verb used here.

clue.text: Dodgy announcer tainted, to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A broadcaster whose reputation has been partly sullied.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy in the sense of risky or not to be relied on means doubtful.

clue.text: Foul feud ref's put up with

indicators.note: foul means corrupt or bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A referee enduring a nasty quarrel on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffered means tolerated or endured, the same as put up with.

clue.text: Strip? Kinky nurses do, almost

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order
almost means the short verb loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A saucy hint about what nurses nearly get up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off one's clothes, which is the verb meaning disrobe.

clue.text: Plot upsetting in Hamlet? I suppose

indicators.note: upsetting says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters wanted are tucked inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone guessing that the play in question is Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is the indicator of the hidden word; 'upsetting' then turns ETIS round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land, a piece of ground for building, is a site.

clue.text: Lower chewing cud in grass endlessly

indicators.note: in means the mixed letters are placed within the trimmed plant name
endlessly means the plant name loses its last letter

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass

indicators.note: chewing means the three letters are mashed into a different order

explanation.surface: A cow chewing the cud in a meadow, lowing away.
explanation.walkthrough: REE is REED cut by 'endlessly'; DUC is CUD rearranged by 'chewing'. 'Lower' looks like a mooing cow but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower an amount is to cut it down, the plain sense of the verb.

clue.text: Miles away from wild Moroccan animal

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the remaining letters are jumbled
away from means the abbreviation is taken out of the nationality word

explanation.surface: A wild animal spotted miles from Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M from MOROCCAN leaves OROCCAN, which 'wild' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a North American mammal, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Very bad cut on horse's rear

parts.note: to sever is to cut through

indicators.note: rear means the hindmost letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nasty wound on a horse's hindquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means serious or harsh, as a very bad injury or storm is severe.

clue.text: Commuting fat cats in capital

indicators.note: commuting means changing or exchanging, so the letters swap places

explanation.surface: Wealthy bosses travelling in to work in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, but it is the old adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital as an old-fashioned exclamation of approval means excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Observes lack of publication for teachers?

parts.note: no means none, a lack of something
TES, the Times Educational Supplement, is a British weekly for teachers

explanation.surface: Teachers spotting that their trade paper has stopped appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British newspaper for schoolteachers.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or notice it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Scoundrel, oddly withdrawn, is yet to swear

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible rogue

indicators.note: oddly withdrawn means the first, third and fifth letters are taken away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A rogue, strangely shy, has not yet sworn.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, a synonym for swearing.

clue.text: Cordelia's opening her father's net

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the name

parts.note: Cordelia is the daughter of King Lear in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: Cordelia's first move to land her father in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' is the profit sense, as in to clear a sum after costs.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a sum is to clear it, making that much as profit after expenses.

clue.text: Keep volunteers in check

indicators.note: in means the army letters sit inside the restraining word

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain, so rein means check
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Keeping a band of volunteers under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to go on possessing it, which is exactly what retain means.

clue.text: Reasonable price to follow fashion

indicators.note: to follow means the charge comes after the style word

parts.note: mode means a fashion or style
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Paying a fair price to keep up with fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate and reasonable both describe something not excessive, such as a sensible cost.

clue.text: Editor taken aback by action plan

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: a sign can be a gesture, an action that conveys meaning

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor startled by a plan of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or plan, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Coming and going in transport

definitions.meaning: an arrival, as when an actor comes on stage
a doorway or the act of going into a place
as a verb, to transport is to fill with rapture, to put in a trance

explanation.surface: Arriving and leaving by bus or train.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: two senses of the noun and the verb stressed on its second syllable, meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means an arrival or way in, and the verb means to enrapture, carry away with delight.
